source_precision.detail: The valid bound is <=r B_N for integer r>=1. At r=1, even N and all-one inputs attain equality.
After n=2m several central ranks use n where m is intended; the reconstruction uses ground-set size N and explicit ranks.
One-based first absent index can be r+1; use rank a+d with 1<=d<=r.
Increasing path counts and chain compression are linked through an upward-oriented integral-flow reduction.
Projection scaling, all shadow parities and tie, simultaneous chain replacement, and finite potential termination are explicit.
Assignment multiplicity, open/half-open boundaries, positive integer radii, distinct subsets, large-r truncation and dated conjecture scopes are explicit.

external_input.qualification: Exact later external input for a compilation expansion of the Menger method; not an attribution of Ford1957 to the original1945 paper.

limits: The historical Hilbert, complex boundary-weight and origin-centered lower conjectures are statement pointers; only the real boundary-weight special case is proved here.
No present-day conjecture-status, formal verification, optimal complex constant or arbitrary-small-real-radius bound is asserted.
The original Sperner1928, Konig-book and Littlewood-Offord1943 proofs are not separately reproduced; Sperner's needed conclusion follows from this source's Theorem4.
